parsed.title: Hyperbolic analogue of the Bezdek–Connelly–Kertész average-degree conjecture
parsed.statement:
Let ${\mathcal P}_r$ be a packing of disks of radius $r>0$ in the hyperbolic plane $\mathbb{H}^{2}$, and let ${\rm deg}_{\rm avr}({\mathcal P}_r)$ denote the average degree of its contact graph. **Hyperbolic average-degree conjecture.** For arbitrary such packings,

$$
\limsup_{r\to 0}\left(\sup_{{\mathcal P}_r}{\rm deg}_{\rm avr}({\mathcal P}_r)\right)<5.
$$

This is the still-open hyperbolic counterpart of the corresponding spherical result, which is known.
parsed.source_name: Karoly Bezdek and Muhammad A. Khan, “Contact numbers for sphere packings”, arXiv:1601.00145 (2016).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.00145

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2016).

parsed.title: Identical lists maximize the probability of a non-distinguishing coloring
parsed.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, and let $\mathcal{L}=\mathcal{L}$ be a collection of equal-sized lists, each of size $k$, indexed by the vertices $v
eq 0$ of $G$. Choose a color from each vertex's list uniformly and independently, and let $p(\mathcal{L})$ be the probability that the resulting coloring admits a non-trivial automorphism preserving every color class. **List-probability strengthening.** The probability $p(\mathcal{L})$ is maximized when all the lists are identical. This would strengthen the List Distinguishing Conjecture by identifying the worst-case list assignment for random colorings.
parsed.source_name: Niranjan Balachandran and Sajith Padinhatteeri, “The List Distinguishing Number of Kneser Graphs”, arXiv:1602.03741 (2016).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.03741

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2016).

parsed.title: Closure of co-bipartite unit disk graphs under bipartite complementation
parsed.statement: Let $G$ be a **co-bipartite unit disk graph**, meaning that its vertex set can be partitioned into two cliques, and let the **bipartite complement** of $G$ be the graph obtained by complementing the edges between the two parts while leaving the two cliques unchanged. **Closure conjecture.** For every co-bipartite unit disk graph, its bipartite complement is also a co-bipartite unit disk graph. The conjecture is motivated by the fact that the bipartite complement preserves the unit disk graph property for the subclass whose cross-part edges are $C_4$-free, while the general closure question remains open.
parsed.source_name: Aistis Atminas and Viktor Zamaraev, “On forbidden induced subgraphs for unit disk graphs”, arXiv:1602.08148 (2016).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.08148

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2016).

parsed.title: Acyclicity conjecture for the extra differential on hairy graph complexes with m = -1
parsed.statement:
Let $\mathrm{HGC}_{-1,n}$ be the hairy graph complex with hair degree parameter $m=-1$ and arity parameter $n$, equipped with its standard differential $\delta$ and an extra differential $\Delta$. **Acyclicity conjecture.** For every $n$, the deformed complex is acyclic:

$$
H\left(\mathrm{HGC}_{-1,n},\delta+\Delta\right)=0.
$$

This conjecture concerns the extra differential for odd $m$, whose existence was conjectured in the preceding work; the resulting deformation is intended to make the hairy graph complex acyclic and to support the spectral-sequence method for studying its standard cohomology.
parsed.source_name: Marko Živković, “Differentials on Graph Complexes III - Deleting a Vertex”, arXiv:1602.08316 (2017).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.08316

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2016).

parsed.title: The trace coefficient formula for web-colouring matrices
parsed.statement:
Let $W_n$ denote the web world on size-$n$ objects, and let ${\mathfrak{M}}^{(W(n))}(x)$ be its web-colouring matrix. Write

$$
a(n)=[x^{n-1}]\operatorname{trace}\left({\mathfrak{M}}^{(W(n))}(x)\right).
$$

**Trace coefficient conjecture.** For all $n>1$,

$$
a(n)=\frac{(n-2)!(n^2-3n+4)}{2}.
$$

The values observed for small $n$ agree with a sequence enumerating a class of directed column-convex polyominoes in the plane. A closed formula for the diagonal entries is unavailable because the associated word-reconstruction problem has no known closed-form solution; the proposed formula is supported computationally for the displayed cases.
parsed.source_name: Mark Dukes and Chris D. White, “Web matrices: structural properties and generating combinatorial identities”, arXiv:1603.01589 (2016).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.01589

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2016).

parsed.title: The super-neatness conjecture for finite projective planes
parsed.statement: A finite projective plane is a $2$-design whose parameters satisfy the projective-plane axioms; its incidence graph is the bipartite graph joining each point to the blocks containing it. **Super-neatness conjecture.** Every finite projective plane is super-neat. The source gives no definition of super-neatness in the supplied context, so the precise property being conjectured cannot be stated here.
parsed.source_name: Lang Tang and Shenglin Zhou, “Domination number in block designs”, arXiv:1603.07398 (2016).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.07398

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2016).

parsed.title: Equivariant Kazhdan–Lusztig positivity conjecture for matroids
parsed.statement:
Let $W$ be a finite group acting on a matroid $M$. The equivariant Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial $P_M^W(t)$ has coefficients in the virtual representation ring of $W$. When $M$ is $W$-equivariantly realizable, these coefficients are honest representations.

**Equivariant Kazhdan–Lusztig positivity conjecture.** For every equivariant matroid $W\curvearrowright M$,

$$
P_M^W(t)\in\operatorname{grRep}(W).
$$

Equivalently, all coefficients are honest representations rather than virtual representations. This is known for equivariantly realizable matroids and remains conjectural in the non-realizable case.
parsed.source_name: Katie Gedeon, Nicholas Proudfoot and Ben Young, “The equivariant Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomial of a matroid”, arXiv:1605.01777 (2016).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1605.01777

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2016).

parsed.title: ISR conjecture for line graphs of simple bipartite graphs
parsed.statement:
Let $H$ be a simple bipartite graph, let $L(H)$ be its line graph, and let $V_1,\ldots,V_m$ be a partition of the edge set of $L(H)$. An **independent system of representatives** (ISR) is an independent set meeting each $V_i$ in at most one vertex. **Bipartite line-graph ISR conjecture.** If

$$
|V_i|>\Delta(H)+1
$$

for every $i$, then the system has an ISR. This proposes a stronger ISR property for line graphs of bipartite graphs than for general graphs; the source provides no evidence of a resolution.
parsed.source_name: Ron Aharoni, Eli Berger, Dani Kotlar and Ran Ziv, “On a conjecture of Stein”, arXiv:1605.01982 (2016).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1605.01982

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2016).

parsed.title: Nested-size bipartite rainbow matching conjecture
parsed.statement:
Let $K_{n,n}$ be the complete bipartite graph with $n$ vertices in each part. For bipartite subgraphs $F_1,\ldots,F_k\subseteq K_{n,n}$, a rainbow matching is a choice of pairwise vertex-disjoint edges $e_i\in F_i$.

**Nested-size bipartite rainbow matching conjecture.** If $F_i\subseteq K_{n,n}$ for $i\leq k$ and

$$
|F_i|\geq in
$$

for every $i\leq k$, then $F_1,\ldots,F_k$ have a rainbow matching.

The source presents this as a simpler counterpart of its main bipartite theorem and says that it is believed to be true. Its status is unresolved in the source.
parsed.source_name: Ron Aharoni and David Howard, “A rainbow r-partite version of the Erdős-Ko-Rado theorem”, arXiv:1605.06752 (2016).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1605.06752

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2016).

parsed.title: Bishop comparison conjecture for graphs with nonnegative Bakry–Émery curvature
parsed.statement:
Let $d_{\max}\in{\mathbb N}$. A graph $G=(V,E)$ has vertex degrees $d_x\leq d_{\max}$ for all $x\in V$ and satisfies $CD(0,\infty)$. **Bishop comparison conjecture.** There are constants $C_1,C_2>0$, depending only on $d_{\max}$, such that for every $x\in V$ and $r\in{\mathbb N}$,

$$
|B_r(x)|\leq C_1(1+r^{C_2}).
$$

Thus bounded-degree graphs satisfying $CD(0,\infty)$ should have polynomial volume growth. This is presented as an analogue of Bishop's comparison theorem; the source notes that abelian Cayley graphs provide examples, while the general assertion remains open.
parsed.source_name: David Cushing, Shiping Liu and Norbert Peyerimhoff, “Bakry-Émery curvature functions of graphs”, arXiv:1606.01496 (2017).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.01496

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2016).

parsed.title: The cycle-with-loops homomorphism-density conjecture
parsed.statement:
Let $G$ be a $d$-regular simple graph. Let $C_n^o$ be the graph obtained from the cycle $C_n$ by adding a loop at each vertex, and let $p_H(G)$ denote the normalized homomorphism density from $G$ to $H$.

**Cycle-with-loops conjecture.** For every $ne4$,

$$
p_{C_n^o}(G)\leq p_{C_n^o}(K_{d+1}).
$$

This conjecture extends the known extremal inequalities for particular target graphs and predicts that the complete graph maximizes these homomorphism densities among $d$-regular simple graphs.
parsed.source_name: Emma Cohen, Péter Csikvári, Will Perkins and Prasad Tetali, “The Widom-Rowlinson model, the hard-core model and the extremality of the complete graph”, arXiv:1606.03718 (2017).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.03718

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2016).

parsed.title: Cross-confluence of reduction for Artin-Tits monoids
parsed.statement:
Let $M$ be an Artin–Tits monoid and let $\mathcal{R}_{M}$ be its reduction system on multifractions. Two multifractions are **right reducts** of the same multifraction if they are obtained from it by sequences of right reductions; the system is **cross-confluent** when any two such reducts admit a common left reduct. **Cross-confluence conjecture.** For every Artin–Tits monoid $M$, the system $\mathcal{R}_{M}$ is cross-confluent.

Cross-confluence would imply semi-convergence and thus provide a route to the word problem without requiring ordinary convergence. The paper presents it as its main conjecture, supported by examples and computations, but no general proof is given.
parsed.source_name: Patrick Dehornoy, “Multifraction reduction II: Conjectures for Artin-Tits groups”, arXiv:1606.08995 (2017).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.08995

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2016).

parsed.title: The weak closure property for matroids over hyperfields
parsed.statement:
Let $F$ be a hyperfield and let $\mathcal{M}$ be an $F$-matroid with vector set $\mathcal{V}^*(\mathcal{M})$. The **Weak Closure Property** is the assertion that, for all $X,Y\in \mathcal{V}^*(\mathcal{M})$, one has

$$
(X\boxplus Y)\cap \mathcal{V}^*(\mathcal{M})\neq \emptyset.
$$

**Weak Closure Property.** The Weak Closure Property holds for all matroids over hyperfields. This would characterize a broad class of tract-like coefficient systems for which vector sets retain a weak form of additive closure; the supplied text does not indicate whether the assertion is proved or remains open.
parsed.source_name: Laura Anderson, “Vectors of matroids over tracts”, arXiv:1607.04868 (2018).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1607.04868

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2016).

parsed.title: Larsen–Shalev conjecture for automorphic word maps
parsed.statement:
Let $w$ be a nonempty reduced word in $d$ distinct variables, let $S$ be a nonabelian finite simple group, and let $\mathfrak{P}_w(S)$ denote the relevant automorphic word-map quantity. 

**Larsen–Shalev conjecture.** For each such word $w$, there exist constants $N(w),\eta(w)>0$ such that, for every nonabelian finite simple group $S$ with $|S|\geq N(w)$,

$$
\mathfrak{P}_w(S)\leq |S|^{d-\eta(w)}.
$$

This is presented as the direct automorphic-word-map analogue of Larsen and Shalev's result for ordinary word maps. The statement is intended to follow from an adaptation of their proof, but the bounded-rank Lie-type case remains open because field automorphisms can make the defining degrees of fibers unbounded.
parsed.source_name: Alexander Bors, “Fibers of automorphic word maps and an application to composition factors”, arXiv:1608.00131 (2016).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1608.00131

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2016).

parsed.title: Failure of automorphism invariance for Andrews–Curtis equivalence
parsed.statement: Let $F_2$ be the free group on $x,y$, let ${\mathcal B}_2$ be the set of balanced presentations of the trivial group with two generators, and let $\operatorname{Aut}(F_2)$ act componentwise on pairs. Write $(u,v)\sim_{\operatorname{AC}}(u',v')$ when the pairs are related by Andrews–Curtis moves. **Failure of automorphism invariance.** It is not true that for every $(u,v)\in{\mathcal B}_2$ and every $\varphi\in\operatorname{Aut}(F_2)$, one has $(u,v)\sim_{\operatorname{AC}}(\varphi(u),\varphi(v))$. This contradicts the possibility that adding automorphism moves never enlarges Andrews–Curtis orbits for all balanced presentations. The source gives no resolution evidence beyond the asserted negative statement.
parsed.source_name: Dmitry Panteleev and Alexander Ushakov, “Conjugacy search problem and the Andrews-Curtis conjecture”, arXiv:1609.00325 (2016).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.00325

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of September 2016). “It is widely believed that the Andrews�Curtis conjecture is false with most theoretic works attempting to disprove it.”

parsed.title: Rush–Shi's cyclic sieving conjecture for exceptional minuscule posets
parsed.statement: Let $P$ be one of the two minuscule posets associated to an exceptional Lie algebra of type $E$, and let $k\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$. Write ${\mathsf{PP}}^k(P)$ for the plane partitions of height at most $k$ over $P$, let $\Psi$ denote rowmotion on this set, and let $f_P^k(q)=\sum_{\mathcal{I}\in{\mathsf{PP}}^k(P)}q^{|\mathcal{I}|}$. **Rush–Shi's conjecture.** The polynomial $f_P^k$ is a cyclic sieving polynomial for the action of $\Psi$ on ${\mathsf{PP}}^k(P)$. This extends the cyclic sieving phenomenon previously known for minuscule plane partitions of height at most $2$ to the exceptional type $E$ cases for every nonnegative height.
parsed.source_name: Holly Mandel and Oliver Pechenik, “Orbits of Plane Partitions of Exceptional Lie Type”, arXiv:1712.09180 (2018).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.09180

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2017).

parsed.title: Lattice conjecture for inverse atom sets of involutions in the symmetric group
parsed.statement:
Let $S_n$ be the symmetric group, let $\mathcal{I}(S_n)$ denote its set of involutions, and for $z\in\mathcal{I}(S_n)$ let $\mathcal{A}(z)$ be the corresponding set of atoms, equipped with the atomic order $<_A$. **Lattice conjecture.** If $z\in\mathcal{I}(S_n)$, then

$$
(\mathcal{A}(z)^{-1},<_A)
$$

is a lattice. This is presented as a related conjecture about the additional structure of atomic orders; determining the sets $\mathcal{A}(z)$ efficiently for involutions in arbitrary Coxeter groups remains an open problem.
parsed.source_name: Zachary Hamaker and Eric Marberg, “Atoms for signed permutations”, arXiv:1802.09805 (2025).
parsed.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2017–2018). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1709.07996](https://arxiv.org/abs/1709.07996).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.09805

Status: **open** according to the source (as of February 2018). “It is an open problem to efficiently determine the sets $\cA(z)$ when $z$ is an involution in an arbitrary Coxeter group.”

parsed.title: Induced-matching avoidance conjecture for partial edge colorings of hypercubes
parsed.statement: Let $Q_d$ be the $d$-dimensional hypercube, and let $varphi$ be a partial $d$-edge coloring of $Q_d$. A **color class** is the set of edges receiving one fixed color, and an **induced matching** is a matching whose endpoints induce no additional edges of $Q_d$. A partial coloring is **avoidable** if some proper $d$-edge coloring of $Q_d$ assigns a different color to every precolored edge than the one prescribed by $varphi$. **Induced-matching avoidance conjecture.** If $d\ba3$ and every color class of $varphi$ is an induced matching, then $varphi$ is avoidable. The paper proves this when $d$ is a multiple of $3$, while conjecturing the statement for every $d\ba1$; the supplied candidate is the stronger formulation with $d\ba3$.
parsed.source_name: Carl Johan Casselgren, Per Johansson and Klas Markström, “Avoiding and extending partial edge colorings of hypercubes”, arXiv:2104.00716 (2021).
parsed.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2017–2021). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1711.01066](https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.01066).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.00716

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of April 2021). “Note further that such a statement as in Conjecture does not hold for general $d$-regular (bipartite) graphs.”

parsed.title: Kündgen–Ramamurthi's weak 4-choosability conjecture for planar graphs
parsed.statement: A list assignment $L$ of a graph is **symmetric** if its colours are integers and, for every vertex $v$ and integer $i$, $i\in L(v)$ implies that $-i\in L(v)$. A graph is **weakly $k$-choosable** if it is $L$-colourable for every symmetric list assignment $L$ in which each list has size $k$. **Kündgen–Ramamurthi's conjecture.** Every planar graph is weakly $4$-choosable. This is stated as a strengthening of the Four Colour Theorem and was proposed by Kündgen and Ramamurthi; it remains open.
parsed.source_name: Xuding Zhu, “List 4-colouring of planar graphs”, arXiv:2203.16314 (2022).
parsed.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2017–2022). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1711.02848](https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.02848).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.16314

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2022). “The following conjecture, which is a strengthening of the Four Colour Theorem, was proposed by K\"{u}ndgen and Ramamurthi and remains open.”

parsed.title: Ustimenko's eigenvalue conjecture for Lazebnik–Ustimenko–Woldar graphs
parsed.statement:
For prime powers $q$, let $D(k,q)$ be the graph whose bipartite double cover is $CD(k,q)$. The nontrivial eigenvalues of these graphs are compared with the quantity $2\sqrt q$.

**Ustimenko's conjecture.** For all $(k,q)$, every nontrivial eigenvalue of $D(k,q)$, and therefore of $CD(k,q)$, is at most $2\sqrt q$.

This spectral bound would yield improved upper bounds on $H_n(C_{2k})$ through the pseudorandomness of $CD(k,q)$. The source notes that known cases give the resulting bound for some small values, while proving sufficiently useful cases for larger $k$ remains open; even weaker eigenvalue bounds could suffice.
parsed.source_name: John Byrne and Michael Tait, “Improved upper bounds on even-cycle creating Hamilton paths”, arXiv:2304.02164 (2023).
parsed.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2017–2023). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2207.04629](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.04629), [arXiv:1701.03685](https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.03685).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.02164

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2023).
